description: We are The J-SONs, a multidisciplinary engineering team combining software development, chemical process design, mechanical analysis, and electrical engineering. Our passion lies in applying real-world engineering principles, hardware integration, and data science to space exploration challenges.
summary: We built an interactive dashboard that centralizes the most important information from microgravity combustion studies in one place, supporting fire prevention in space. It shows the number of studies under a default category and a summary of processed data, making it easy to find similar studies based on the variables a user cares about. We used Python (Pandas and NumPy) and use firts SAFFIRE-I, II, and III experiments, which cover the most important variables. Gemini was used for the visual design and Claude to integrate the code. As extras, we added a chatbot that answers questions about the stored data and a glossary for people unfamiliar with the technical terms.
details:
We chose the flame challenge because we found it interesting how something so common to us can change drastically under different environmental conditions, and also because it can cause a major disaster if not studied or understood well. Our panel functions as a repository of NASA research (PSI Data), where you can find studies that interest us according to our variables of interest. While reviewing the published resources, we came across PSI-98, PSI-99, and PSI-100, which correspond to the SAFFIRE I, II, and III experiments, where the large-scale fire propagation speed under low-gravity conditions is determined using material samples like SIBAL, PMMA, and PMMA with Nomex. PSI-25, PSI-26, PSI-69, and PSI-68 were also added, which deal with topics very close to fire prevention in zero gravity.

Once the variables were classified, 30,000 data files were cleaned and then dashboard mockups were integrated. After that, support for the chatbot (Flamita) based on Ollama was programmed, and we ended up optimizing the data shown on the panel to make it more accessible.

Among the benefits of our dashboard is that we provide a thorough exploration of the data from NASA's PSIs, which makes it easier to use in our own research. It becomes a simpler way to review experiments and model the data. The main ideas for the dashboard were sketched out with Gemini and then finalized with Cloude. For creating the chatbot "Flamita," we thought about people who aren’t very familiar with the topic of flames in microgravity, so they can ask Flamita any question on the subject or quickly check out the research.
